# Weak hash MD5 or SHA-1 (Go)

`qualor:go/weak-hash` · Security hotspot · Severity: Low · [CWE-328](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/328.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A04:2025 Cryptographic Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A04_2025-Cryptographic_Failures/), [A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A02_2021-Cryptographic_Failures/)

> **Security hotspot.** This rule asks for a review: it marks code that is often safe and
> sometimes not, and a person decides which. A hotspot never fails the quality gate.

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Use of the MD5 and SHA-1 hash functions: `md5.New`, `md5.Sum`, `sha1.New`, `sha1.Sum`, and
`crypto.MD5.New()` / `crypto.SHA1.New()`, also when the package is imported under another name.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
MD5 and SHA-1 are broken: anyone can make two inputs with the same hash on purpose. Where the hash
protects something (a password, a signature, a token, a check that a file was not tampered with),
an attacker can forge a match.

Many uses are harmless, though: a checksum against accidental corruption, a cache key, or an id
required by a protocol such as git. Only a person can tell which case applies, so this is a
hotspot.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** an API key is stored as its MD5 hash, so a forged match would pass.

```go
package keys

import (
	"crypto/md5"
	"encoding/hex"
)

func Fingerprint(apiKey string) string {
	sum := md5.Sum([]byte(apiKey))
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}
```

**Compliant:** SHA-256.

```go
package keys

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
)

func Fingerprint(apiKey string) string {
	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(apiKey))
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- For signatures, tokens and integrity checks against tampering, use SHA-256 or better
  (`crypto/sha256`, `crypto/sha512`), or an HMAC with such a hash.
- For passwords, use a password hashing function (`golang.org/x/crypto/argon2`, `bcrypt` or
  `scrypt`), never a plain hash.
- If the hash only detects accidental changes or serves as a cache key, the code can stay as it
  is.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `crypto/md5`
- `crypto/sha1`
- `crypto`

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Hash functions passed as values to another API (`hmac.New(sha1.New, key)`, the hash parameter of
  a key derivation function) are not reported; only calls of `New` and `Sum` are.
- A local variable that shadows the package name (`md5 := x; md5.Sum(b)`), or another package
  named `md5` or `sha1` imported under an alias next to the standard one, is taken for the hash
  package.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
